problems.description: 18 convention violations across index.ts, generator.test.ts, server.test.ts: classes/interfaces not using PascalCase and constants not UPPER_CASE, driving the convention score to 0.59.
SonarQube cognitive complexity +50 across only +5 new functions implies over-nested control flow in the new modules, a smell worth refactoring in a later session.

strengths: Greenfield commit follows an idiomatic TS+jest layout (ts-jest preset, node environment, test roots scoped to src/).
Tests are committed alongside the implementation (generator.test.ts, server.test.ts), not deferred.
Committing package-lock.json pins transitive dependencies for reproducible installs.
Session-1 scope is minimal and focused on scaffolding with no architectural over-engineering.
commit_reviews.summary: Idiomatic greenfield scaffolding that only stumbles on naming conventions (score 0.59, 18 PascalCase/UPPER_CASE violations) and mildly elevated cognitive complexity, both minor and easily addressed in later story sessions.

problems.description: SonarQube reports +2 code smells; the new setupTemplateDir helper duplicates the setupContentDir pattern, and repeated fs.rmSync cleanup blocks could be hoisted into an afterEach.

Measured convention score 0.59 is driven by 18 'PascalCase/UPPER_CASE' findings that are false positives (HTML/CSS class names and constants inside template-literal fixtures in generator.test.ts/server.test.ts/index.ts, not TypeScript classes). Qualitative review found no genuine naming violations.

strengths: Extends buildSite with a templatesDir parameter consistent with the existing contentDir/outputDir pattern
Tests mirror the established setupContentDir helper and tmpdir lifecycle conventions exactly
Thorough coverage of edge cases: custom layout via frontmatter, fallback to default, partials, and template data rendering
No new bugs, no duplication (0.0%), and cognitive complexity decreased by 10
commit_reviews.summary: Well-structured feature addition that follows existing patterns and broadens test coverage, with the low measured convention score being a false-positive artifact from HTML class names inside template literals.

problems.description: 18 naming-convention violations in new files (index.ts, generator.test.ts, server.test.ts) — classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE; SonarQube convention score 0.59. Note: several are in test files where the PascalCase/UPPER_CASE rules commonly produce false positives, but the mechanical score stands.
Three new runtime dependencies (chokidar, handlebars, ws) added in a single integration session; handlebars may overlap with the existing markdown-it/gray-matter rendering path.
SonarQube reports +2 new code smells, offsetting the otherwise clean delta.

strengths: Lockfile hygiene is correct: transitive deps (anymatch, braces, handlebars, etc.) hoisted and dev/runtime flags flipped consistently with the new runtime dependencies.
commit_reviews.summary: Session 3 integration adds watch/live-reload/templating features with clean lockfile hygiene and no new bugs, but lowers convention adherence to 0.59 (18 naming violations) and expands the dependency surface with three new runtime packages.

compounding_issues: Session 1 committed the entire node_modules tree (plus package-lock and .bin symlinks), bloating the repo; sessions 2 and 3 then committed dist/ build artifacts with no .gitignore discipline
The unrelated seed index.ts (auth API, ~200 LOC) was never removed or wired in, leaving dead code in the tree through all sessions that contradicts the SSG domain
Two parallel rendering systems persist: the original inline HTML builders remain as a fallback path alongside the Handlebars TemplateEngine, duplicating page/index rendering logic
Session 3 dev server silently swallows initial build failures ('Initial build skipped') and injects live-reload only into generated HTML output rather than into the template layer
key_decisions: Greenfield rewrite of the story target (a purpose-built markdown→HTML static site generator) rather than building on the seed, which was an unrelated Express/JWT/SQLite auth API
Modular split (src/generator.ts vs src/cli.ts) plus jest and tsconfig from session 1, establishing the structure that later sessions cleanly extended

Template engine (session 2) implemented as an optional, backwards-compatible extension layer: layouts/partials auto-detected from a templates dir with graceful fallback to inline HTML, so existing tests kept passing
buildSite composition: session 3's dev server reuses buildSite and threads the --templates option through CLI → buildSite → serve, composing layers instead of forking
Live reload built self-contained via a WebSocket server + injected client script (ws + chokidar), avoiding an external reloader dependency
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the three sessions. Session 1 delivered a clean, tested markdown generator (12 tests); session 2 added a well-factored, backwards-compatible Handlebars templating layer that grew coverage to 23 tests without disturbing the initial API; session 3 integrated a dev server with live reload, 11 server tests, and full CLI wiring — ending at 34/34 tests passing. The architecture stayed composable and each session extended rather than rewrote prior work. The arc is marred only by repo hygiene (committed node_modules and dist/, leftover seed index.ts), not by structural decay.
story_review.summary: A coherent, compounding-but-healthy three-session arc that built a tested static site generator, added templating, and integrated a live-reload dev server, with only repo-hygiene debt (committed node_modules/dist and orphaned seed code) detracting from otherwise clean engineering.
